article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Haze × White Widow
Breeder: Dinafem Seeds
THC Content: 17–22%
CBD Content: 0.01–0.2%
Terpene Profile: Terpinolene, beta-myrcene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, pine, cedar, incense, spice, Haze
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid to late October
Indoor Yield: 650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,500 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Few marijuana strains deserve an oversized name as naturally as Moby Dick. Dinafem’s famous Haze and White Widow hybrid was bred around abundance: tall plants, enormous central colas, vigorous branching, heavy resin production, powerful cerebral effects, and yields that can become genuinely impressive when the plant receives enough light and root space. Yet size alone does not explain why this Spanish cultivar became an international classic.

Moby Dick preserves the penetrating incense, citrus, wood, and spice character associated with old-school Haze while White Widow brings denser flowers, trichome production, and enough physical weight to keep the experience from becoming entirely cerebral. Dinafem officially lists the cultivar as 60% sativa and 40% indica, with 17–22% THC, a 60–70-day indoor flowering period, and outdoor plants capable of reaching roughly 3.5 meters under favorable conditions. Over the years, it has accumulated numerous cannabis-cup placements, establishing a reputation that extends far beyond the literary reference in its name.
Genetics and Lineage

The original Dinafem Moby Dick is Haze × White Widow. That pedigree should be stated explicitly because several other breeders have subsequently released marijuana under the Moby Dick name, and not every version is genetically identical. Dinafem’s own strain documentation identifies its cultivar as a sativa-dominant Haze and White Widow cross, with breeder King Kush credited in the company’s historical material as the creator behind the famous selection.

Haze supplies the elongated growth, pronounced flowering stretch, cerebral intensity, incense, citrus, and exotic wood characteristics that define much of the finished plant. White Widow contributes a different set of qualities: thicker flowers, strong resin coverage, sturdy hybrid structure, and a more grounded physical component. The marriage works especially well because neither parent disappears. Mature flower retains unmistakable Haze aromatics, yet its bud density and trichome production are much closer to what growers expect from a high-yielding modern hybrid than from a wispy tropical sativa.

The cultivar’s history also helps separate the original from later reinterpretations. Dinafem documented numerous competition results, including first-place outdoor and indoor-sativa awards and additional placements in Spain, Argentina, and Mexico. Those victories helped establish Moby Dick well before similarly named modern versions appeared. For strain library purposes, the Dinafem Haze × White Widow cultivar remains the historical reference point.
Effects and Experience

Moby Dick is primarily a head-driven strain. The onset can be rapid, producing a sudden increase in mental activity, sensory awareness, and enthusiasm that feels distinctly different from the gradual heaviness of an indica-dominant weed. Music can become more detailed, conversation more animated, and creative tasks unusually absorbing. The cultivar has long been associated with a powerful psychoactive character, and Dinafem went as far as describing the experience as intensely cerebral with near-psychedelic qualities.

That description does not mean every session becomes overwhelming. At moderate doses, the high can feel energetic, cheerful, and mentally expansive, which helps explain the strain’s long-standing popularity for daytime and social use. White Widow becomes more noticeable later, adding a deeper physical calm beneath the cerebral stimulation. The result is not classic couch-lock, but neither is it a completely weightless Haze experience. As the session develops, physical relaxation can soften the sharper mental edge.

Dinafem’s original THC range of 17–22% may look modest beside contemporary flower advertised above 30%, but numerical potency should not be mistaken for subjective intensity. Cannabinoid chemistry, terpene content, individual tolerance, and dosage all influence the experience. Moby Dick can still feel exceptionally strong, especially to people sensitive to stimulating cannabis. Excessive consumption may lead to dry mouth, dizziness, racing thoughts, temporary anxiety, or an uncomfortable sense of mental overstimulation.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers who prefer uplifting cultivars may find Moby Dick more appealing than heavily sedating strains. Its energetic cerebral character may temporarily help some people shift attention away from everyday stress or fatigue, while the accompanying mood elevation can make routine activities feel less burdensome. The later physical component may provide enough relaxation to soften tension without necessarily producing immediate sleepiness.

The strain’s stimulating character deserves equal consideration. Cannabis that feels motivating to one person can feel overly intense to another, particularly at high doses. People who are sensitive to THC-related anxiety or racing thoughts may find a Haze-dominant experience less comfortable than a calmer cultivar with a different cannabinoid profile.

Moby Dick should not be regarded as a clinically proven treatment for depression, anxiety, fatigue, pain, or another health condition. Strain names are not standardized medical formulations, and cannabinoid concentrations vary with phenotype and cultivation conditions. Anyone using marijuana therapeutically should consider the laboratory profile of the actual product, dosage, personal tolerance, medications, and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than relying solely on the cultivar’s reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma is unmistakably rooted in classic Haze. Dinafem describes a penetrating mixture of lemon, spice, incense, cedar, and Haze, with the breeder memorably comparing the fragrance to the wooden pew of an old church. That unusual description captures the profile surprisingly well. There is a dry, resinous, almost antique-wood quality beneath the sharper citrus, while incense and spice provide the unmistakable old-school cannabis character.

Laboratory analysis from Dinafem gives the aroma a chemical foundation. The breeder’s Dinalab report identified terpinolene, beta-myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, beta-pinene, limonene, alpha-pinene, beta-eudesmol, guaiol, eucalyptol, and alpha-humulene among the strain’s principal measured terpenes. Terpinolene can contribute floral, herbal, woody, and citrus-like qualities; limonene reinforces bright lemon; pinene supports the fresh forest character; and caryophyllene adds dry peppery spice.

On the palate, citrus tends to arrive first. Lemon peel and pine give way to incense, cedar, herbs, and spice, leaving a dry Haze-like finish that can linger after the smoke or vapor has cleared. A careful cure can reveal sweeter or slightly floral nuances underneath the woodiness, but Moby Dick remains fundamentally different from contemporary cannabis dominated by fruit candy, cake batter, or creamy dessert flavors.
Growing Information

Moby Dick’s enormous production potential comes with one important condition: the plant needs resources. Dinafem describes the cultivar as easy to grow in terms of overall resilience but exceptionally demanding when it comes to light, nutrients, water, and physical space. Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days, with breeder yields reaching about 650 grams per square meter. Outdoors, plants can reach roughly 3.5 meters and produce up to 1,500 grams each in ideal conditions, with harvest occurring from mid to late October.

Vertical stretch requires planning. Dinafem warns that the plant expands aggressively after flowering begins and even recommends limiting indoor vegetative growth to around three weeks when space is restricted. Topping, low-stress training, or a SCROG -style canopy can make far better use of indoor light than allowing one unrestricted main stem to race toward the ceiling. Wide internodal spacing improves light penetration, while numerous vigorous branches provide the framework for surprisingly heavy flower production.

Nutrient demand is another defining characteristic. The plant can consume more fertilizer and water than lighter-feeding cannabis genetics, particularly when strong lighting drives rapid growth. That does not justify blindly increasing nutrient concentration; growers should monitor the plant and root zone rather than feeding according to reputation alone. Outdoors, Moby Dick performs best when given abundant soil volume, direct sunlight, and a warm temperate or Mediterranean-style season. Dinafem also notes good resistance to humidity, an advantage for a plant capable of developing extremely large colas. Despite their weight, branches are naturally sturdy and can often support mature flowers without extensive staking.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Moby Dick?
The original Dinafem Moby Dick is Haze × White Widow. Dinafem officially identifies the strain as a sativa-dominant hybrid containing approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica genetics.
Is Moby Dick indica or sativa?

Moby Dick is sativa-dominant. Dinafem lists it as 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its effects are correspondingly cerebral and stimulating, although the White Widow side contributes noticeable physical relaxation later in the experience.
How strong is Moby Dick?

Dinafem gives an original THC range of approximately 17–22% and CBD levels of about 0.01–0.2%. Despite not carrying the extreme THC percentages associated with some newer weed strains, Moby Dick has a reputation for unusually intense and long-lasting psychoactive effects.
What does Moby Dick taste like?

Expect lemon, pine, cedar, spice, incense, herbs, and unmistakable Haze. Rather than modern candy sweetness, its profile is dominated by citrus, resinous wood, and incense-like aromas associated with classic sativa genetics.
How long does Moby Dick take to flower?
Dinafem lists an indoor flowering period of 60–70 days. Outdoor plants typically finish between mid and late October in the Northern Hemisphere.
Final Thoughts on Moby Dick

Moby Dick earned classic status by exaggerating nearly everything growers valued in its parents. Haze contributes soaring cerebral effects, incense, citrus, wood, and enormous growth, while White Widow adds resin, density, stability, and enough physical influence to make the experience more rounded. Dinafem combined those qualities into marijuana capable of producing huge colas without sacrificing the aromatic identity that made European Haze strains famous.

Its cultivation numbers remain impressive even by modern standards: up to 650 g/m² indoors, around 1,500 g per plant outdoors, a 60–70-day flowering period, and outdoor plants potentially reaching 3.5 meters. More importantly, those figures are backed by a long history of competition recognition rather than appearing solely as promotional specifications. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in strains from before the modern dominance of Cookies, Gelato, and Runtz genetics, Moby Dick offers a very different experience—lemon and incense instead of frosting, vigorous Haze energy instead of instant couch-lock, and a plant whose sheer scale makes the white-whale name remarkably appropriate.
